value.title: RunState grammar + careful-mode chat spawn + /careful toggle
value.description: Lay the spine for chat-driven approval. Extend the RunState status grammar additively with 'input-required' and 'paused' plus optional pending/pause fields. Add an additive `bober run --approve-gates <comma-list>` flag that merges {gate -> 'disk'} into config.pipeline.checkpointOverrides for that run only. Add a session-persisted `/careful on|off` toggle (chat sidecar) and make RunSpawner pass the curated `--approve-gates post-research,post-plan,post-sprint` to the detached child when careful is on. After this sprint a chat user can launch an approval-gated run whose curated gates actually fire pending markers, while autopilot spawns are unchanged.

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build) and typecheck is clean in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass with zero failures, including new tests for the grammar extension, --approve-gates parsing, and the /careful toggle (npm run test).

RunState.status accepts 'input-required' and 'paused' and the optional fields pendingCheckpointId/pendingPrompt/pendingSince/pausedAt round-trip through writeRunState/readRunState. A unit test writes a RunState with status 'input-required' + pending fields and reads it back unchanged; an existing-status RunState (running/completed/failed/aborted) still round-trips.

`bober run --approve-gates post-research,post-plan,post-sprint` merges {post-research:'disk', post-plan:'disk', post-sprint:'disk'} into config.pipeline.checkpointOverrides for that run; without the flag, checkpointOverrides is left as-is (today's behavior). A unit test asserts the merge and asserts an unknown gate name (not a declared checkpoint id) is rejected with a clear error.

`/careful on` / `/careful off` persists the careful flag in a chat-scoped sidecar across turns; `/careful` with no arg reports the current state. A unit test toggles and re-reads the sidecar via a fresh instance.

When careful is on, RunSpawner.spawn launches the detached child with `--approve-gates post-research,post-plan,post-sprint` appended to the args; when off (default), no --approve-gates is present and the args equal Phase 1's exactly. A unit test inspects the injected spawnFn args in both states.

nonGoals: Do not surface pending approvals in chat yet (read path is Sprint 2)
Do not write approve/reject markers from chat yet (write path is Sprint 3)
Do not add guidance injection or pause/resume (Sprints 4 and 5)
Do not modify the DiskCheckpointMechanism, approval-state.ts, or the existing approve/reject CLI
Do not change autopilot spawn behavior or the pipeline algorithm
stopConditions: A careful chat spawn launches with the curated --approve-gates; an autopilot spawn is byte-for-byte unchanged from Phase 1; the RunState grammar extension round-trips; build + typecheck + full suite green
value.definitionOfDone: RunState gains 'input-required'/'paused' and the optional pending/pause fields (additive, round-tripping). `bober run` gains an additive --approve-gates flag that merges disk overrides for the named gates only, rejecting unknown gate names. A session-persisted /careful on|off toggle exists, and RunSpawner passes the curated approve-gates to the detached child when careful is on while leaving autopilot spawns identical to Phase 1. Build, typecheck, and the full suite pass.
assumptions: The set of valid checkpoint ids is the pipeline's declared sites (post-research, post-plan, post-sprint-contract, post-sprint, pre-curator, pre-generator, pre-evaluator, pre-code-reviewer, end-of-pipeline). The validator for --approve-gates checks membership in this set.
The careful sidecar is keyed by sessionId and lives under .bober/chat/ (mirrors src/chat/pid-sidecar.ts). Default state is off (autopilot), preserving Phase 1.
Merging into checkpointOverrides (override wins over mode) is sufficient to activate only the curated gates without setting --mode careful.

value.title: Surface pending approvals in chat (read path) + roster input-required
value.description: Make a blocked run visible in chat. Add an ApprovalReader over .bober/approvals/*.pending.json (reusing approval-state.ts list helpers), an announce-once dedupe cursor (mirroring the CompletionTailer/cursor-store pattern), and a poll-prelude in the chat turn that weaves a 'run <id> is waiting at <gate>: <prompt>' notice into the reply. The roster / `/runs` output shows the correlated run as [INPUT-REQUIRED], and the pending checkpoint id/prompt are reflected onto the chat-owned RunState so /runs is consistent across turns. Read-only: this sprint never writes approval markers.

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass, including new ApprovalReader, dedupe-cursor, and chat-surfacing tests (npm run test).

ApprovalReader.read() returns the pending markers from .bober/approvals/*.pending.json (checkpointId, runId, prompt, requestedAt). A unit test with two synthetic pending markers (one with a runId, one without) returns both; a corrupted JSON file in the dir is skipped silently; a missing dir returns [].

When a pending marker correlates (by runId) to a running chat run, handleTurn weaves a one-time notice naming the runId, checkpoint id, and rendered prompt into the reply. A unit test injects a synthetic pending marker + matching running RunState and asserts the notice text appears in the turn output.

Announce-once dedupe: a given pending marker (keyed by checkpointId+requestedAt) is surfaced at most once across turns; a still-pending marker does not re-announce on the next turn. A unit test runs two turns against the same marker and asserts the notice appears only on the first.

The roster summary / `/runs` shows a correlated run as [INPUT-REQUIRED] and the chat-owned RunState gains pendingCheckpointId/pendingPrompt/pendingSince + status input-required. A unit test asserts both the summary line and the persisted RunState fields.
With no pending markers present, chat behavior is identical to Phase 1 — no spurious notices and the existing chat-session/roster tests stay green.

nonGoals: Do not write .approved.json / .rejected.json from chat (Sprint 3)
Do not add guidance injection or pause/resume (Sprints 4 and 5)
Do not modify the DiskCheckpointMechanism or approval-state.ts write functions
Do not clean up markers on completion yet (Sprint 6 hygiene)
stopConditions: A blocked run is surfaced once in chat and shown [INPUT-REQUIRED] in /runs; no-pending behavior is unchanged; build + typecheck + full suite green
value.definitionOfDone: Chat surfaces pending approvals: an ApprovalReader over the approvals dir, an announce-once dedupe cursor, a poll-prelude notice in handleTurn, [INPUT-REQUIRED] in the roster, and the pending fields reflected onto the chat-owned RunState. Read-only — no markers are written. With no pending markers, behavior matches Phase 1. Build, typecheck, and the full suite pass.
assumptions: Correlation is by the pending marker's optional runId field (PendingMarker.runId, approval-state.ts:27) matched against running RunStates from RosterReader. A marker with no runId is surfaced as 'unknown run' but still announced (so a CLI-spawned careful run is not silently hidden).

Because marker files are checkpointId-keyed in a shared dir, at most one careful chat run is expected at a time this phase; correlation ambiguity from concurrent careful runs is the documented limitation (handled in Sprint 6 docs).

The dedupe cursor mirrors src/chat/cursor-store.ts and is stored per session under .bober/chat/; identity key = checkpointId + requestedAt (stable while pending, changes if the gate is re-requested in a later round).

value.title: Resolve approvals from chat: /approve, /reject + feedback, NL
value.description: Close the human-in-the-loop. Add `/approve <checkpointId>` and `/reject <checkpointId> [feedback]` slash commands plus natural-language approve/reject intent (via the existing loose-JSON classifier) that write .approved.json / .rejected.json markers by reusing saveApproved/saveRejected with the pendingExists guard and resolveApprover. The detached child's DiskCheckpointMechanism poll then resumes automatically; rejection feedback flows into the pipeline's runCheckpointWithFeedback rework round. After resolution the chat-owned RunState clears its pending fields and returns the run to running on the next poll.

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass, including new approve/reject slash, NL-classify, and marker-write tests (npm run test).

`/approve <checkpointId>` for an existing pending marker writes .bober/approvals/<id>.approved.json with approverId from resolveApprover() and acks resumption; for a non-existent pending marker it returns a clear 'no pending checkpoint' message and writes nothing. A unit test asserts both (file written / not written) using the pendingExists guard.

`/reject <checkpointId> <feedback>` writes <id>.rejected.json carrying the feedback string (and rejecterId). A unit test asserts the rejected marker contents; a separate test confirms the DiskCheckpointMechanism reads that marker and resolves to {approved:false, feedback:<feedback>} (reusing the existing mechanism, not a reimplementation).

Natural-language approval/rejection is classified to an approve/reject action carrying the target checkpoint id (resolved from the single outstanding pending marker, or the one named in the message) and routed to the same handlers. A unit test drives a stubbed classifier returning approve/reject and asserts the correct marker is written; when the target is ambiguous (multiple pending, none named) the turn asks which checkpoint instead of writing.

After a marker is resolved, the chat-owned RunState clears pendingCheckpointId/pendingPrompt/pendingSince and reflects the run back to 'running' on the next poll. `/help` lists /approve and /reject. A unit test asserts the RunState transition and the updated help text.

nonGoals: Do not reimplement the disk poll/resume — the detached child's DiskCheckpointMechanism already resumes when the marker appears
Do not change the existing approve.ts/reject.ts CLI commands
Do not add guidance injection or pause/resume (Sprints 4 and 5)
Do not change how the pipeline consumes rejection feedback (verify the existing runCheckpointWithFeedback path; do not modify it)
stopConditions: Approving/rejecting from chat writes the correct marker, a blocked run resumes via the existing disk poll, reject feedback reaches the rework path, and RunState clears its pending fields; build + typecheck + full suite green
value.definitionOfDone: Chat can resolve a pending checkpoint: /approve and /reject slash commands plus NL intent write the .approved.json/.rejected.json markers (reusing saveApproved/saveRejected, pendingExists guard, resolveApprover); the detached child resumes via its existing disk poll; reject feedback reaches runCheckpointWithFeedback; RunState clears pending fields and returns to running. /help updated. Build, typecheck, and the full suite pass.
assumptions: saveApproved/saveRejected (approval-state.ts:106,122) and resolveApprover (cli/commands/approve.ts:29) are reused directly; resolveApprover may be lifted/exported so the chat handler shares it (or duplicated as a tiny env read if importing the CLI module is undesirable).

When a single pending marker is outstanding, NL approve/reject targets it implicitly; when several are outstanding, the handler requires the checkpoint id (asks the user) rather than guessing — consistent with the 'never guess a load-bearing target' discipline.

Resume is the existing DiskCheckpointMechanism poll in the detached child (disk.ts:104-169); chat only writes the marker and acks. The RunState running-flip is observed by the chat poll on a later turn (it is fine if the ack says 'resuming' before the child's next poll tick).

value.title: Free-text guidance injection: /tell <runId> <text> + pipeline read point
value.description: Let a human steer a run with free-text guidance, not just approve/reject. Add a runId-keyed guidance channel (.bober/runs/<id>/guidance.jsonl) appended by `/tell <runId> <text>` (and NL 'tell run X to …'), and an ADDITIVE pipeline read point that, at each checkpoint boundary, drains pending guidance for the active runId and injects it as extra context into the next agent (curator/generator) handoff. With no guidance present the pipeline behaves byte-for-byte as before (the pipeline.ts:571 invariant).

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass, including new guidance-channel, drain, and pipeline-injection tests (npm run test).

`/tell <runId> <text>` for a known run appends a guidance entry {ts, text, consumed:false} to .bober/runs/<runId>/guidance.jsonl and acks; for an unknown run it returns a clear error and writes nothing. A unit test asserts the appended entry and the unknown-run no-op. A runId containing path separators or '..' is rejected before any write.

A guidance helper drains pending (unconsumed) guidance for a runId — returning the entries and marking them consumed so a second drain returns nothing. A unit test asserts drain-then-redrain semantics on the JSONL channel.

The pipeline drains and injects pending guidance for the active runId at a checkpoint boundary, threading the drained text into the next agent's context/handoff. A unit/integration test seeds guidance for a runId and asserts the boundary read point surfaces it into the agent input (via a stubbed agent invocation or the handoff object).

The pipeline read point is purely additive: with no guidance file present, the pipeline produces the same handoff/agent input as before and the existing pipeline test suite stays green. A unit test asserts no-guidance is a no-op (no change to the handoff).

Natural-language 'tell run X to <instruction>' is classified to a tell action {runId, text} and routed to the /tell handler. A unit test with a stubbed classifier asserts the guidance entry is written. /help lists /tell.

nonGoals: Do not mutate an agent call already executing — guidance applies only at the NEXT checkpoint boundary
Do not change phase order or the pipeline algorithm; the read point is additive only
Do not add pause/resume (Sprint 5) or hygiene/docs (Sprint 6)
Do not require careful mode — guidance can be queued for any run, but is only drained at boundaries that execute
stopConditions: Guidance can be queued from chat and is drained+injected at a pipeline boundary; no-guidance is a verified no-op; build + typecheck + full suite green
value.definitionOfDone: A runId-keyed guidance channel exists, /tell (slash + NL) appends to it with path-safety + unknown-run guard, a drain helper marks entries consumed, and an additive pipeline boundary read point injects drained guidance into the next agent handoff. With no guidance, the pipeline is byte-for-byte unchanged. /help updated. Build, typecheck, and the full suite pass.
assumptions: guidance.jsonl is append-only with one JSON object per line {ts, text, consumed?}; 'drain' rewrites the file (or appends a consumed-marker) atomically via the temp-file+rename pattern used in run-state.ts:41-52. The exact consumed-tracking representation is the generator's call as long as drain-then-redrain returns nothing the second time.

The natural injection boundary is the per-sprint pre-generator/pre-curator handoff and/or the post-sprint boundary, where the pipeline already builds a handoff object and invokes an agent (pipeline.ts around the curate/generate sites). Injecting drained guidance text as an extra context field on that handoff is sufficient; the generator chooses the least-invasive insertion point that is provably additive.
The active runId is available inside runPipeline via the existing opts.runId path (run.ts:155 threads --run-id into runPipeline). Guidance is keyed by that same runId.
outOfScope: Guidance that edits files or overrides the contract (only adds advisory context)

value.title: Soft pause / resume: /pause, /resume + paused RunState + cooperative gate
value.description: Add a soft suspend that keeps the process alive — distinct from the already-built hard /stop (kill-by-PID). `/pause <runId>` (and NL) writes a runId-keyed pause marker (.bober/runs/<id>/paused.json) and flips the chat-owned RunState to 'paused'; an ADDITIVE cooperative-pause check at each checkpoint boundary blocks (polls) while the marker is present; `/resume <runId>` removes the marker and the run continues, RunState returning to 'running'. With no pause marker, the boundary is unchanged beyond a single existence check.

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass, including new pause-marker, cooperative-gate, and resume tests (npm run test).

`/pause <runId>` for a running run writes .bober/runs/<runId>/paused.json, flips the chat-owned RunState to 'paused' (with pausedAt), and acks that the process stays alive (distinct from /stop). A unit test asserts the marker, the RunState transition, and that no kill signal is sent. /pause on an unknown or non-running run returns a clear message and writes nothing.

The pipeline's additive cooperative-pause check blocks (polls) at a checkpoint boundary while paused.json exists and proceeds once it is removed. A unit/integration test with an injected clock/poll asserts the boundary does not advance while paused and advances after the marker is cleared.

`/resume <runId>` removes paused.json and flips RunState back to 'running'. A unit test asserts the marker is gone and the status transition; the cooperative gate then advances. /help lists /pause and /resume.

The cooperative-pause check is additive: with no pause marker, the boundary behaves as before (single existence check, no added blocking) and the existing pipeline suite stays green. Natural-language pause/resume intent is classified and routed to the handlers. A unit test asserts no-marker no-op and NL routing via a stubbed classifier.

nonGoals: Do not kill the process — that is the existing hard /stop (Phase 1)
Do not change phase order or the pipeline algorithm; the pause check is additive only
Do not pause mid-agent — the cooperative gate only acts at checkpoint boundaries
Do not add hygiene/docs/e2e (Sprint 6)
stopConditions: A run can be soft-paused and resumed from chat, holding at the next boundary while paused; no-marker is a verified no-op; build + typecheck + full suite green
value.definitionOfDone: Soft pause/resume works: /pause (slash + NL) writes a runId-keyed pause marker and flips RunState to paused without killing the process; an additive cooperative-pause check blocks at the next boundary while the marker is present; /resume removes it and the run continues with RunState back to running. With no marker, the boundary is unchanged. /help updated. Build, typecheck, and the full suite pass.
assumptions: The cooperative-pause check reuses the disk-poll pattern from DiskCheckpointMechanism (disk.ts) — a bounded setTimeout poll loop with an injected clock for deterministic tests; a sane upper bound (reuse approvalTimeoutMs or a dedicated cap) prevents an unbounded hang.

The pause check is placed at the same checkpoint boundaries used for guidance (Sprint 4) and approvals, so 'paused' behaves like 'held at the next gate' rather than an instantaneous freeze of in-flight work.

RunState 'paused' (added in Sprint 1) is owned/written by the chat process; the pipeline only reads the paused.json marker to decide whether to block. Resume is observed by the chat poll which flips RunState back to running.
outOfScope: Pausing in the middle of an agent invocation

value.description: Harden and document the mid-flight HITL loop. Clean up stale pending/guidance/pause markers and chat-owned RunState pending/paused fields when a run completes or is aborted. successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
